intended_object: A complex representation ρ of G on V is realizable over ℝ: it is the complexification of a real representation. Equivalently, in a suitable basis every ρ(g) is a real matrix (Serre §13.2, Isaacs Ch. 4). This is read off the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body asks for a real representation σ on ℝ^n, with n = finrank ℂ V, together with a ℂ-linear isomorphism e : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] ℝ^n ≃ V such that e(1 ⊗ σ g w) = ρ g (e(1 ⊗ w)) for all g and w. The pure tensors 1 ⊗ w span ℂ ⊗ ℝ^n over ℂ, so this condition is the same as e intertwining the base change of σ with ρ. The library proves this as `isRealForm_iff_nonempty_equiv`. So the predicate says exactly that ρ is isomorphic to the complexification of a real representation of dimension dim_ℂ V, which is the textbook notion of realizability over ℝ for finite-dimensional representations.

Fixing the carrier to ℝ^n loses nothing when V is finite-dimensional, because any real form has real dimension dim_ℂ V and so transports to ℝ^n. When V is infinite-dimensional, finrank is 0 and the predicate is false. The docstring says so openly, and realizability over ℝ in Serre and Isaacs is a notion about finite-dimensional representations, so this is no real discrepancy. The general carrier-free version is also in the library, as `IsRealForm`.

Generality: G is any monoid, which is more general than the finite groups of the literature. Restricting to the pair ℂ/ℝ is part of the notion itself, which is the setting of the Frobenius–Schur indicator. A general "realizable over a subfield" notion would be a different definition. Mathlib's `Representation.baseChange` exists, but I found no Mathlib predicate for real forms or realizability.
